About a week later he came to my home and gave me some books
to read, which I later realised were of a communistic nature.
He visited me again on March 29, 1933 and brought a few more
books of a communist nature for me to read. I do not
know where he resides and I have not seen him since that
date.

Regarding the other books which were found in my room,
I bought them either in Nanking or in Shanghai. My reason
for buying them was because I was interested in social and
economic affairs and I was under the impression that these
volumes would assist me in the study of political economy.

My relatives with whom I was living know nothing of
my affairs and are in no way connected with subversive
elements.

I am not a communist and am not affiliated to any party
neither have I ever been approached by anyone to join any
radical society.

Subject (in full) Case against Seng Ching Tao (孙靖涛), Zeng Lee (任濂),
and Zeng Seng Sz (任双氏) arrested by the Municipal Police
on 31.3.1933.
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by [签名]

Regarding the case against Seng Ching Tao, Zeng Lee and
Zeng Seng Sz, who were arrested by the Municipal Police on the
night of March 31, 1933 at 402 Z Bu Li (慈厚里), Hardoon
Road on the authority of a warrant issued at the request of
the Public Safety Bureau, I have to state that the first two
accused have been subjected to a lengthy interrogation by D.S.
Pitts and Clerk Van Ti-Foo, but no further evidence which would
materially assist in strengthening the case against them has
been obtained.

The first accused - Seng Ching Tao - admits possession of
the communistic literature which was found in his room, and
states that he himself purchased a great deal of it in either
Shanghai or Nanking, with the object of assisting him in his
study of political economy. He denies however, being a
communist or being affiliated to any political party and further
states that his sister and brother-in-law - the third and second
accused - knew nothing about the red literature being in his
room. A statement made by the 1st. accused is attached
herewith.

A statement made by the second accused is also forwarded.
This man is an accountant at the National Commercial Bank Ltd.
78 Peking Road and has been employed there for fourteen years
and according to the management of this institution bears a
good record. Nothing has come to light which would indicate
that this individual is in any way connected with subversive
activities.

Regarding the third accused - Zeng Seng Sz - who is at
present detained in the cells of the Special District Court, a
statement will be taken from her and forwarded later.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
D. S.

关于孙靖涛、任濂和任双氏一案，此三人系根据公共安全局（Public Safety Bureau）的请求所签发的搜查令，于1933年3月31日晚在哈同路（Hardoon Road）慈厚里（Z Bu Li）402号被工部局警务处逮捕。兹声明，前两名被告已由 D.S. Pitts 和书记员范蒂福（Van Ti-Foo）进行了长时间的审讯，但并未获得能实质性地加强针对他们的案件证据的进一步材料。

第一被告——孙靖涛——承认拥有在其房间内发现的共产主义文献，并声称其中大部分是他为了辅助学习政治经济学而在上海或南京自行购买的。然而，他否认自己是共产党员或隶属于任何政党，并进一步声称他的姐姐和姐夫——即第三和第二被告——对他房间内有红色文献一事毫不知情。第一被告的供词附后。

关于第三被告——任双氏（Zeng Seng Sz）——她目前被羁押在特区地方法院的拘留所中，将对其录取供词并随后转呈。

特务科主管警官。

My name is Seng Ching Tao (孫靖濤) alias Sung Sao Lai (孙少莱)
alias Siau Moh ( 小毛 ), 21, single native of Hangchow. My
address in Hangchow is Chih Woo Zoe Kuen Hua Sz Road ( )
near the Sing Sz Market.

I first studied at a primary school in Hangchow from the
age of 6 and remained there until I was 17, after which I
continued my studies at the Wen Hua College ( 文化 ), Nanking
until I was 20.

I came to Shanghai on January 10 of this year 1932 with the
object of securing employment here. Upon my arrival I made
my way to the downstairs room of 402 Z Eu Li ( 慈厚里 ), Har-
door Road which was leased by my brother-in-law Zeng Lee (任廣),
who has been living there with his wife for the last two years.

About a month after my arrival in Shanghai I read an ad-
vertisement to the effect that a teacher was required at the
Ming Tso ( 民族 ) Primary School, K'ong Joh Li, Sinza Rd.
I applied for and obtained the position which consisted of
teaching very young children the rudiments of Chinese and kindred
studies. My salary in this job was $20 per month. Up
till the time of my arrest I was employed at this school.

About a fortnight ago I went to the Law College on Rue
Prosper Paris in order to see an old school mate of mine named
Wu Vung Tsu ( 吳文周 ). I met Wu and at the same time
I was introduced by one of his acquaintances to a man named Luk
who was also visiting friends at the College. Lu and I
talked together about social conditions and the corruptness
of the Kuomintang. We talked in this vein for some time and
eventually I gave him my address and asked him to visit me.

以下为孙靖涛（孫靖濤），别名孙少莱（Sung Sao Lai），别名小毛（Siau Moh）（ ）的供词，系杭州籍人士，由我 L. C. Pitts 于1932年4月2日在静安寺捕房（B. W. Station）录取，并由书记员范思福（Van Si Foo）传译。

我叫孙靖涛（孫靖濤），别名孙少莱（Sung Sao Lai），别名小毛（Siau Moh）（ 小毛 ），21岁，单身，杭州籍。我在杭州的住址是兴市市场附近的芝乌佐坤华寺路（Chih Woo Zoe Kuen Hua Sz Road）（ ）。

我从6岁起在杭州的一所小学读书，直到17岁，之后我在南京文华学院（Wen Hua College）（ 文化 ）继续求学，直到20岁。

我于今年1932年1月10日来到上海，目的是在此寻找工作。抵达后，我前往哈同路（Hardoon Road）慈厚里（Z Eu Li）（ 慈厚里 ）402号的楼下房间，该房间由我的姐夫任广（Zeng Lee）（任廣）租赁，他和妻子过去两年一直住在那里。

我到上海约一个月后，看到一则广告，称新闸路孔佐里（K'ong Joh Li）明佐（Ming Tso）（ 民族 ）小学招聘教师。我申请并获得了该职位，工作内容是教授幼童中文基础及相关科目。我在这份工作中的薪水是每月20元。直到被捕时，我仍受雇于该校。

大约两周前，我去霞飞路（Rue Prosper Paris）的法学院看望一位名叫吴文周（Wu Vung Tsu）（ 吳文周 ）的老同学。我见到了吴，同时通过他的一位熟人介绍，认识了一位名叫陆（Luk）的男子，当时他也正在学院拜访朋友。陆和我交谈了社会状况以及国民党的腐败问题。我们以此类话题交谈了一段时间，最后我给了他我的地址，并请他来拜访我。
